design.concept: A single-column, one-thing-at-a-time expense tracker. The person lands on their expense list (status chips, stacked records with amount and status), taps one to read it like a memo (identity, amount, dates, description, rejection reason), and meets the send or resend actions at the very end of that reading. Registering and correcting are side tasks that open as their own steps with a back control.

views.purpose: Primary view: filter chips by status, the stacked list of own expenses with date, category, amount and status, load more, and a clear entry point to register a new expense.
Read the open expense top to bottom (identity, decisive facts, narrative, rejection reason, resubmission trail), then the send or resend block at the end.
Single-column form to register a new expense (date, category, amount, description). On success the created draft opens in the detail view, where the person can send it.
Single-column form prefilled from the rejected expense, with the manager's reason on top. Saving returns to the detail, where resubmission is the last beat.

design.decisions: I used the scene host in scenary mode, so every view change goes through it. There are four scenes instead of one shared form scene, because the page holds no state. 'novo' and 'correcao' are the two form modes, each bound to its own draft and command. The page follows the readAndDecide template: the detail reads identity, facts, narrative, then the actions block at the end, with no sticky bar. Failures show above the buttons in body colour and keep the drafts. The success statement is calm and local. The list uses the preferred vertical record list, with status chips as a wrapping group, not a horizontal scroller, and 44px+ targets. Money and dates are only formatted with Intl, never computed. The draft money string is converted to a number only for the money input. Opening an expense switches the scene first and shows the card loading while obterDespesa runs. After registering or saving a correction, the page returns to the detail only when the command status is success. The proof attachment has no field in the contract or the shared state, so I left the file upload out rather than show a control that stores nothing. The 'Reenviar' action only appears for a rejected expense not yet resent (the reenvioRealizado flag), and 'Enviar' only for drafts, both read from backend fields.
